task_reconstruction.official_task: Build a sustainability measure, compare countries, and propose a development plan for one unsustainable country.

section_map.summary: Summary splits sustainability into two dimensions and names the winner program.
Ecological footprint is presented and then rejected for ignoring economy and society.
Sustainable distance is defined as angle times projection, threshold 0.7854.
Five countries are scored and Nepal is called unsustainable.
The same Nepal distance is called sustainable, reversing the verdict.
The modernization program wins on both measures.

contributions.summary: A geometric sustainability score: angle between actual and ideal direction, times the projection onto the diagonal.
Entropy and CRITIC weights combined only after a Kendall consistency test.

dependency_graph.handoff: the footprint idea, extended to two axes
the sustainable distance and its threshold

assumptions.summary: The measured country is stable: extremely dramatic change does not happen.
The ideal development direction is the diagonal of the unit square.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Four indices dropped for lack of data.
Missing values imputed with the R packages mi and mice.

models.summary: Footprint minus carrying capacity, the rejected baseline.
Sustainable distance as angle times projection, threshold 0.7854.
ARIMA forecast and a system-dynamics intervention model.

verification.summary: Five countries scored over 2003 to 2012 against one threshold.
Kendall consistency test and Spearman post hoc check on the two weight sets.

results_trace.summary: France 0.570225 smallest, then South Africa 0.685853, America 0.764749, Nepal 1.114179, China 1.401829.
Nepal called sustainable because its distance exceeds the threshold. This reverses the page 11 verdict and the inequality. Both readings kept.
Modernization program: distance 0.848138, 0.977041, 0.955021, 0.272045 at five-year steps.

writing_logic.summary: Standard model stated, then the omission named, then the replacement built.
Each failing country gets its own cause.
Simpler model rejected by naming the data property that breaks it.

language_observations.summary: The summary names both dimensions before any formula.
The threshold is written as a product of two chosen numbers, with the result shown.
The winner is declared only after it leads on both measures.

visualization_observations.summary: The country is placed in the unit square, ideal direction drawn as the diagonal.
Table 2 lists all five distances to the same number of decimals.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The ranking table makes every verdict checkable against one threshold.

independent_extensions.summary: Estimate the two threshold factors instead of choosing pi over 3 and 0.75.

candidate_rule_impacts.impact: Two indices on one scale with a stated threshold written as a product.
A borrowed production function with one term dropped and a reason given.
Two weight sets combined only after a consistency test.
Dropped indices and imputed values are both named.
Five countries compared against one threshold, with one internal contradiction recorded.
Each proposal carries cost, political demand and a decision.
Indices ranked by the difference quotient of the distance.
ARIMA chosen after ARMA is rejected for seasonality.
The stability assumption is stated and then glossed.
The summary splits the concept before the formula.
Two failures get two separate causes.

unresolved_questions: Page 11 calls Nepal unsustainable at distance 1.114179. Page 13 calls Nepal sustainable because the distance exceeds the threshold. Both readings are recorded; neither is corrected.
The printed formulas are images; the recorded equations are reconstructed from the prose.
